articles.title: Australia has been galvanised by ‘melon-gate’. So what is the luxury fruit at the centre of the PM’s controversy?
articles.excerpt:
Shizuoka Crown melons are part of an important cultural gifting practice in Japan, where they are hand-patted by growers to achieve an even shape and texture

The melons at the centre of a national im...
articles.body_text:
Shizuoka Crown melons are part of an important cultural gifting practice in Japan, where they are hand-patted by growers to achieve an even shape and texture

The melons at the centre of a national imbroglio involving the Australian prime minister have the sweetness of a watermelon, the snap of a honeydew and the perfume of a peach, according to fruit sellers.

Anthony Albanese maintains he has nothing to apologise for, after a joke he made regarding a gift he received from Japan’s prime minister.

While Albanese is facing scrutiny over his comments – and hand gestures – the fruit in question has received less attention. They are not only a prized delicacy but are a part of a significant Japanese cultural practice.

According to Melbourne fruitier Thanh Truong, also known as Fruit Nerd, there is a culture of fruit gifting in Japan that does not exist in Australia.

“We don’t have a culture of spending money on fruit like they do in other parts of the world,” Truong said. This is because, in Australia, fruits are understood as a “commodity”, something that should be priced accessibly for everyone, he said. Shizuoka Crown melons are a luxury good – priced between $50 and $150 a piece.

A variety of the muskmelon family, whose other members include rockmelon and the honeydew, they have become a prized gift in Japan due to the care involved in growing them. This process involves being hand-patted by growers, to give the fruit an even shape and exterior pattern.

Truong said that, for growers, “their attempt at perfection” is part of the fruit-gifting culture.

There is also only one crown melon grown per vine, which Truong said gives them maximum nutrients and a higher sugar level. Truong describes the taste as: “The sweetest watermelon you’ve had, with the texture of a honeydew and the perfume of the strongest kind of rockmelon or peach.”

In Japan, these efforts reflect the level of respect shown to the gift’s recipient. The melon is also supposed to give the recipient health and wealth, Truong said. This is very different to gifting somebody alcohol, which is more typical in Australia, he said.

Graham Gee, a senior buyer at the Happy Apple in Melbourne, said that in Australia we have year-round access to honeydews, rockmelons and other varieties of the muskmelon. But in Japan, the melon market is “very seasonal”, making it a “special occasion” when they do arrive.

The import of fresh melons from Japan into Australia was permitted at the beginning of this year, though melons from the Okinawa prefecture are still banned. But neither Gee nor Truong have yet to see them being sold locally.

“There is a beauty to it, and not everyone can appreciate it,” Truong said.

articles.title: Seahawks sign former first-round Lions cornerback Terrion Arnold despite looming felony charges
articles.excerpt: Kansas City Chiefs Passing Game Coordinator said that Patrick Mahomes’ knee issues are "non existent" entering Training Camp. Nick Wright, Chris Broussard, and Kevin Wildes ask if the Chiefs will boun...
articles.body_text:
Kansas City Chiefs Passing Game Coordinator said that Patrick Mahomes’ knee issues are "non existent" entering Training Camp. Nick Wright, Chris Broussard, and Kevin Wildes ask if the Chiefs will bounce back in 2026, and if Aaron Donald could have an impact on the Los Angeles Rams after having a formal tryout.

Terrion Arnold, the former Detroit Lions first-round pick, is no longer a free agent.

Arnold and the Seattle Seahawks have reached a deal to bring him into the fold with the reigning Super Bowl champions, according to multiple reports.

The Lions, who selected Arnold with their first-round pick in 2024, released him in June after he was arrested in Tampa, Florida, on felony charges connected to a robbery and kidnapping from February.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Terrion Arnold, No. 0 of the Detroit Lions, stands on the sidelines during the national anthem before an NFL game against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on Dec. 5, 2024, in Detroit, Mich. (Getty Images)

The Seahawks were among the teams, though, that Arnold visited earlier this week as he looked for his next chapter in the league. He also visited with the Houston Texans, New York Giants and New Orleans Saints.

But the Seahawks, which already touts a superb defense on paper, are who Arnold wants to play with next. In fact, during HBO’s "Hard Knocks," GM John Schneider was even seen discussing the potential of signing Arnold to their roster.

Head coach Mike Macdonald also noted the "great tryout" Arnold had while in Seattle.

LIONS RELEASE TERRION ARNOLD AFTER BOND SET AT $1 MILLION IN ARMED ROBBERY, KIDNAPPING CASE

"It’s a situation where there’s other things that are surrounding it," Macdonald told reporters this week. "We’re aware of that. But we’re working through the situation right now. But it was a great visit. I really enjoyed meeting him, and I think he enjoyed being here, so we’ll see where it goes."

Arnold is facing eight felony charges stemming from the allegations that he orchestrated the abduction and beating of three men in February.

Prosecutors said in June that Arnold arranged for the men to be pistol-whipped after he suspected them of stealing $100,000 in cash and luxury goods from him. He was described as the "primary conspirator" of the incident, and Hillsborough County Judge Christopher Sabella set his bail at $1 million.

Terrion Arnold of the Detroit Lions runs onto the field before an NFL game against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan, on Nov. 27, 2025. (Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images)

However, Arnold’s attorney, R. Timothy Jansen, said in Hillsborough County court this summer that his client will be "absolutely denying these allegations." His agency, EAG Sports Management, added there is "no credible evidence" against him in this case.

Lions head coach Dan Campbell also noted in March that the team did not believe Arnold was involved in this case based on the information they had at the time.

Teams that were looking into adding Arnold to their roster needed to do their due diligence on the matter. No trial date has been set in his case.

The charges against him carry a sentence of up to life in prison. And for the NFL, they must decide whether Arnold should be placed on the commissioner’s exempt list.

If a team is willing to sign him now, it must mean he should be free to play, at least at some point, this season.

Terrion Arnold of the Detroit Lions looks on during the second half of an NFL game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wis., on Sept. 7, 2025. (Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images)

Arnold was expected to be a starting corner for the Lions this season, making his release a big one for the depth chart. He recorded his first career interception this past season in Week 9 against the Minnesota Vikings, though he was only able to play eight games because of a shoulder injury that required season-ending surgery.

Arnold played 16 games during his rookie season in 2024, tallying 10 passes defended and 60 combined tackles.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Follow Fox News Digital’s sports coverage on X and subscribe to the Fox News Sports Huddle newsletter.

Scott Thompson is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Marco Rubio gets 68 new jobs in epic White House birthday gift inspired by viral meme
articles.excerpt:
President Trump gives recognition to Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the State of the Union.

Marco Rubio has a lot of jobs. Now, he has 68 more.

The White House gave the secretary of state a gold-...
articles.body_text:
President Trump gives recognition to Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the State of the Union.

Marco Rubio has a lot of jobs. Now, he has 68 more.

The White House gave the secretary of state a gold-framed collage for his 55th birthday featuring dozens of versions of the viral "Rubio realizing" meme that has transformed President Donald Trump’s top diplomat into everything from an Iranian ayatollah to an astronaut.

At the center of the 68-panel mosaic is the original, unaltered photograph of Rubio slumped on a couch in the Oval Office earlier this year, signed by Trump in gold ink with a presidential endorsement: "You are great."

WHAT RUBIO’S RISE AS THE INTERNET’S 'FIXER' TELLS US ABOUT TODAY’S POLITICS

President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky meet in the Oval Office at the White House on Feb. 28, 2025, in Washington, D.C., to sign a preliminary agreement on sharing Ukraine's mineral resources. Trump said the agreement will allow America to recoup aid provided to Kyiv while supporting Ukraine's economy. (Getty Images)

Around it is a resume that rivals Barbie's.

There’s Rubio as Robocop, Rubio as an astronaut, Rubio as the White House Easter Bunny, Cardinal Rubio preparing for a papal conclave, Rubio bundled up as the leader of Greenland, and one where Rubio holds up a sign that says, "Please stop making memes about me."

The White House presented Rubio with the collage in May, but the gift only came to wider attention this week after Axios reporter Marc Caputo shared a photo of it on X.

While nearly 70 imaginary gigs may sound excessive, the joke lands particularly well for a Cabinet official who has already accumulated an unusually high number of real ones.

VANCE, CRUZ, HEAD TO IOWA ON 2026 MISSIONS AS 2028 GOP RACE TO SUCCEED TRUMP HEATS UP

Vice President JD Vance speaks during a meeting with President Donald Trump, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Secretary of State Marco Rubio in the Oval Office at the White House on Feb. 28, 2025, in Washington, D.C. Trump and Zelensky are meeting to negotiate a preliminary agreement on sharing Ukraine's mineral resources that Trump says will allow America to recoup aid provided to Kyiv while supporting Ukraine's economy. (Getty Images)

Rubio serves as secretary of state as well as acting national security advisor, and previously pulled double duty as acting archivist and acting administrator of the U.S. Agency for International Development.

The internet also appears to have decided Rubio could handle a few more.

The meme began with a decidedly more serious moment on Feb. 28, 2025, when Trump, Vice President JD Vance, Rubio and other administration officials met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in the Oval Office.

A photograph from the contentious meeting captured Rubio sitting low on a couch, his hands interlocked and an expression on his face that the internet quickly interpreted as a man coming to an uncomfortable realization.

HOW MARCO RUBIO IS RIDING LAUGHTER AND MEMES TO SOCIAL MEDIA DOMINANCE

Then came the heavily-Photoshopped memes. As major jobs opened, in reality or otherwise, Rubio kept getting hired.

When Venezuela's Nicolás Maduro was captured, meme Rubio appeared dressed to take over the country. When Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz announced he would not seek re-election, Rubio turned up in blaze-orange hunting gear, shotgun included.

Rubio has acknowledged that he wasn't initially thrilled with the photograph that launched it all.

"The meme thing, you know, was interesting, 'cause when it first came out, I hated that picture," Rubio recently told Lara Trump on Fox News' "My View."

MARCO RUBIO SPOTTED IN NIKE TRACKSUIT ABOARD AIR FORCE ONE DURING TRIP TO CHINA, IGNITING MEMES ONLINE

President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky meet in the Oval Office at the White House in Washington, D.C., on Feb. 28, 2025, to sign a preliminary agreement on sharing Ukraine's mineral resources. Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio also attended the meeting. (Getty Images)

Rubio explained that the Oval Office couch was partly to blame.

"If you don't have a pillow behind your back, you kinda sink," he said.

But the secretary of state eventually surrendered to the court of public opinion.

"And then it turned into this other thing and it was fine, and it's funny," Rubio said.

He also revealed that Scavino had turned the online frenzy into something framed forever.

"Dan Scavino made a nice board for me," Rubio said. "And even since he made that board, we had to update it."

Which raises an obvious problem — Rubio may already need a bigger frame.

The White House and the State Department did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

Jasmine Baehr is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital, where she covers politics, the military, legal debates surrounding life and family policy, as well as faith and culture.

articles.title: UAE accuses Iran of attacks on two ADNOC vessels in Strait of Hormuz
articles.excerpt:
The United Arab Emirates has condemned Iran for attacking two ships linked to the UAE’s national oil company in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) confirmed that “two of...
articles.body_text:
The United Arab Emirates has condemned Iran for attacking two ships linked to the UAE’s national oil company in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) confirmed that “two of its vessels were attacked while transiting” the waterway on Thursday evening, adding that the situation was “brought under control”, Emirati media reported.

“The United Arab Emirates has strongly condemned and denounced the hostile Iranian attack that targeted two vessels affiliated with ADNOC as they transited the Strait of Hormuz,” the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement in the early hours of Friday.

No injuries were reported from the attack, the ministry added.

Iran did not immediately comment on the attack or the UAE’s claims.

The attack comes just days after the UAE reported a similar attack on an ADNOC tanker on Saturday.

Iran is continuing to uphold an effective blockade on the Strait of Hormuz, and wants to charge users for passage. The United States fiercely opposes this plan and has instituted its own blockade on Iranian shipping.

Iran is currently in talks with Oman over arrangements for the strait’s future management.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has previously threatened action against any vessels transiting the strait if they are linked to Tehran’s adversaries, or if they fail to comply with Iranian directives.

The Emirati Foreign Ministry said attempts by Iran to use the Strait of Hormuz as a tool of economic coercion amount to “piracy”, and constitute a “direct threat to the stability of the region, its peoples, and the global energy supply”.

After the attack on the ADNOC ship on Saturday, the UAE blamed the IRGC for the strike.

That attack, which also caused no injuries, drew condemnation from regional and Arab governments.

ADNOC reports that a total of 15 of its vessels have been attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz since the start of the US-Israel war on Iran in February.

OutKick host Dan Dakich joins Stuart Varney to break down the potential $12.5 billion sale of the Los Angeles Lakers to Kushner and Iger, the WNBA's statement on transgender eligibility, and Donald Trump's Super Bowl predictions.

Major League Baseball and Netflix almost pulled off something truly special on Thursday night.

The MLB at Field of Dreams matchup between the Philadelphia Phillies and Minnesota Twins delivered a pregame sequence that gave baseball fans chills. Watching current players from both squads emerge from the iconic Iowa cornfield alongside 26 Hall of Famers, including all-time greats like Cal Ripken Jr., Mike Schmidt, Joe Mauer and Jim Thome, was cinematic gold.

Then, Netflix cut back to the pregame desk, and the spell was instantly broken.

BASEBALL FANS FUME AT MLB'S 'FIELD OF DREAMS' GAME DECISION, REPORTER TRICIA WHITAKER HAS A BOAT DAY & LLWS!

Whatever goodwill the entrance generated was shattered the moment lead anchor Elle Duncan started talking. Instead of letting the historic backdrop breathe, viewers got wooden delivery, forced commentary and little genuine baseball insight. Social media was unforgiving, skewering her appearance from the moment she went live.

Elle Duncan attends the Netflix 2026 Upfront red carpet at Sunset Pier 94 Studios on May 13, 2026, in New York, N.Y. (Variety via Getty Images)

"@netflix had options for the #FieldofDreamsGame and we get the insufferable Elle Duncan. Damn," one frustrated viewer posted on X.

Another echoed: "What dirt does Elle Duncan have on Netflix? Every word out of her mouth is insufferable."

The pushback isn't coming out of nowhere. Duncan has given baseball diehards plenty of reason to question her baseball chops and why Netflix continues putting her front and center for marquee events.

NETFLIX REPLACES FAN-FAVORITE FOOTBALL HOST WITH UNPOPULAR, FAR-LEFT PERSONALITY

This is the same host who, during Netflix's Opening Day broadcast from Oracle Park earlier this season, famously referred to home plate as "home base."

That broadcast drew plenty of criticism for Duncan's awkward, forced delivery, too. Thursday night wasn't exactly a course correction.

The Philadelphia Phillies and Minnesota Twins take the field before a game at Field of Dreams in Dyersville, Iowa, on Aug. 13, 2026. (Getty Images)

Beyond the terminology blunders, fans are exhausted by Duncan’s reputation for bringing lecture-heavy narratives into sports coverage.

Look no further than her recent commentary regarding WNBA star Caitlin Clark. Instead of sticking to the action on the court, Duncan opted for the soapbox: "It’s not on her to be burdened by social media clowns," she said, before adding, "As much as we would love for you to be able to just focus on that (basketball)… it’s unfortunately not your reality."

NETFLIX CO-CEO CLARIFIES STREAMING GIANT’S LIVE SPORTS STRATEGY AMID NFL LINEUP EXPANSION, FEDERAL SCRUTINY

Major League Baseball set the stage, but Netflix's choice of host proved the streamer still has a long way to go in understanding what sports fans actually want to see.

Former MLB players are celebrated on the field before a game between the Philadelphia Phillies and the Minnesota Twins at Field of Dreams in Dyersville, Iowa, on Aug. 13, 2026. (Getty Images)

Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

Alejandro Avila is a longtime writer at OutKick, living in Southern California.

articles.title: HHS warns Texas hospitals against denying life-saving care to newborn with disability
articles.excerpt: Fox News correspondent Madeleine Rivera reports on a legal battle involving surrogate mother McKenna West, who traveled to Texas to give birth after refusing the intended parents' request to abort the...
articles.body_text:
Fox News correspondent Madeleine Rivera reports on a legal battle involving surrogate mother McKenna West, who traveled to Texas to give birth after refusing the intended parents' request to abort the baby over a congenital heart condition diagnosis.

The Trump administration is stepping into the battle over a Texas newborn with a severe heart defect, warning two hospitals they cannot withhold medical treatment because of his disability.

The Department of Health and Human Services’ Office for Civil Rights told Fox News Digital on Thursday that it is sending a letter to Children’s Medical Center of Dallas and UT Southwestern Medical Center outlining their obligations under federal disability civil rights laws as doctors make treatment decisions involving baby Gabriel.

The federal intervention comes after Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton took action to ensure the newborn receives medically necessary care following a dispute that began when his biological parents allegedly asked their surrogate to abort him after he was diagnosed with hypoplastic left heart syndrome.

SURROGATE GIVES BIRTH IN TEXAS TO BABY WITH HEART DEFECT AFTER PARENTS REQUESTED ABORTION

Surrogate mother McKenna West, who fled to Texas after her baby's birth parents allegedly asked her to abort the child (Live Action)

Surrogate mother McKenna West refused the request and traveled to Texas, where Gabriel was born Wednesday and taken to a neonatal intensive care unit.

In its letter, HHS' civil rights office makes clear that federal law prohibits withholding medical treatment based on a person's disability, including based on judgments that the life of someone with a disability has less value or that the individual would impose a burden on others.

Those federal protections extend to decisions involving life-sustaining treatment, according to HHS.

The agency said it is monitoring Gabriel's case and offering technical assistance to Children’s Medical Center of Dallas and UT Southwestern as the hospitals determine his care.

HHS OFFICIAL WARNS OF IRREVERSIBLE RISKS AS TRUMP ADMIN RESTRICTS FUNDING FOR YOUTH GENDER PROCEDURES

Newborn baby boy in a small transparent portable hospital bed. (iStock)

HHS is also urging the hospitals to seek a review by an infant care committee if doctors consider withholding or withdrawing medically indicated treatment. The agency said life-sustaining treatment should continue during that review.

The federal action marks the latest intervention in the dispute over Gabriel's medical care.

West was around 20 weeks pregnant when Gabriel was diagnosed with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, a congenital condition in which the left side of the heart is severely underdeveloped. The diagnosis allegedly prompted the intended parents to ask West to have an abortion, according to Paxton's office.

West instead traveled to Texas, and Paxton formally notified UT Southwestern Medical Center and Children’s Medical Center of Dallas of what his office said were their legal obligations to provide Gabriel with "medically necessary, life-saving care upon birth."

TEXAS AG PAXTON DEMANDS DALLAS SHERIFF PURSUE ICE AGREEMENT AS DEADLINE DISPUTE SPARKS LEGAL THREAT

July 29, 2015: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton speaks during a hearing in Austin, Texas. ( )

Paxton later secured a court order aimed at ensuring the baby received care after birth.

"The court has made the right decision in immediately acting to protect baby Gabriel’s life and ensure he receives the care he deserves," Paxton said.

"My office utilized every tool at our disposal to protect life, and we will not back down in continuing to support baby Gabriel’s well-being," he added. "Every child in our state deserves to be cared for and protected, and that’s exactly what I’ll fight for."

The case has drawn an outpouring of support for West from conservative and pro-life advocates, who praised her decision to continue the pregnancy and fight for Gabriel's care.

SUPREME COURT UNANIMOUSLY SLAPS DOWN BLUE STATE TARGETING PRO-LIFE GROUP

Andrew Kolvet, a spokesman for Turning Point USA, called West a "hero" on X, writing that she "saved this baby's life" and saying he hopes she is ultimately able to keep Gabriel.

Alliance Defending Freedom, which represents West, celebrated the court order requiring Gabriel to receive the surgery. ADF Senior Counsel Erik Baptist praised West's "courageous stand" for Gabriel and said "every child deserves a chance at life."

Pro-life group Live Action also praised West for resisting pressure to abort Gabriel, but said the fight is not over. The group raised concerns that a court order is preventing West from having contact with the newborn, saying Gabriel "needs the comfort of the only mother he's ever known" and that his needs should remain the priority.

Gabriel was born Wednesday and brought to a neonatal intensive care unit, where doctors could perform surgery to treat his heart condition.

"Baby Gabriel deserves a chance at life, and I will not allow anyone to unlawfully deny him medically necessary care," Paxton previously said. "My office will use every tool available to protect innocent lives and ensure that every child receives the care required under Texas law."

Fox News Digital reached out to Children’s Medical Center of Dallas and UT Southwestern Medical Center for comment.

Fox News Digital's Robert McGreevy contributed to this report.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

articles.title: Iran could unleash ‘kinetic’ response as US tightens economic containment, analyst warns
articles.excerpt: Tensions escalate between the U.S. and Iran as President Donald Trump demands billions in compensation for decades of damages. Sanctions strategist Miad Maleki analyzes Iran's collapsing economy and t...
articles.body_text:
Tensions escalate between the U.S. and Iran as President Donald Trump demands billions in compensation for decades of damages. Sanctions strategist Miad Maleki analyzes Iran's collapsing economy and the impact of the administration's maximum pressure campaign. Sandra Smith hosts the discussion detailing oil export drops and rising economic misery under tight U.S. sanctions.

Iran could launch military strikes as early as this fall, targeting a list of high-value assets to shatter increasing U.S. economic sanctions, national security analysts warned Thursday.

The warning came as the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company, or ADNOC, reported that two vessels were struck transiting the Strait of Hormuz, according to the United Arab Emirates' state-run WAM news agency.

ADNOC said there were no injuries and the situation was under control, according to Reuters, and as the UAE foreign ministry condemned the Iranian attacks.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also said Thursday that Washington was preparing to take unprecedented economic action against Iran.

"Watch this ⁠space for more announcements ​coming next week because we ​are going to apply measures like have never been seen in ​the history of economic ​isolation on a country," Bessent said in ‌an ⁠interview on Newsmax.

Iranian forces could shift to guerrilla-style hit-and-run attacks to exploit the U.S. troop buildup in the Gulf. (Photo by AFP via Getty Image)

Behnam Ben Taleblu, a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital that Tehran is likely to step up military pressure as Washington intensifies sanctions.

"Come early fall, what we can expect is for them to kinetically push back against Trump's economic policy," Taleblu said. "If the president is re-embracing economic pressure as a management approach, just like we saw in 2019, then the regime will use kinetic pressure to try to find a way to break out of that economic containment."

Ben Taleblu said shrinking oil revenues and the U.S. naval blockade could also drive Tehran to expand its target list across the region.

Iranian ballistic missiles are displayed during the ceremony of joining the Armed Forces. Sources are now saying Iran has sent these missiles to Russia. (Iran's Presidency/WANA/West Asia News Agency/Handout/REUTERS)

"This means they would embrace the kinetic tool, and that's how they would get out of the economic containment regime that the U.S. seems to be defaulting to want to put on them," Taleblu added. "I would say more attacks on ships, potentially more attacks on U.S. bases, potentially more attacks on Arab infrastructure in the Persian Gulf, and certainly the regime would create a tiered list of targets of what is of immediate value versus what has greater economic value versus what might lead to the U.S. directly or indirectly responding."

The warnings come amid a deadlock in talks between Washington and Tehran.

So far, there have been no discussions about extending the U.S.-Iran ceasefire agreement, a senior Iranian source told Reuters Aug. 12.

Tehran has insisted Washington return to the pact and set a definitive timeline to meet its obligations.

The interim memorandum of understanding, signed in June, called for the "immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts."

Tehran sent an unprecedented 'whole-regime' team to the US deal talks which signals one priority, a counterterrorism expert said (URS FLUEELER/Pool via REUTERS)

The agreement later unraveled, with Trump declaring on July 7 that the pact was "over."

Under the framework, both sides had an extendable 60-day window to negotiate a final agreement addressing key security concerns, including Iran’s nuclear program.

That deadline expires Aug. 17, with control of the Strait of Hormuz remaining a major sticking point.

Hossein Taeb, the newly appointed head of Iran's Basij paramilitary force, said Thursday that the Strait of Hormuz remains "under Iran's control and management."

His comments conflicted with Trump's assertion a day earlier that the U.S. held "total control" over the vital waterway.

A view of commercial cargo vessels and crude oil tankers are anchored in the Gulf of Oman, off the coast of Muscat, Oman, on June 21, 2026, as they prepare to transit through the critical Strait of Hormuz. Maritime traffic along this vital global trade corridor experienced severe disruptions following heightened geopolitical tensions between the United States and Iran that escalated earlier in February. Following a diplomatic memorandum of understanding reached in mid-June, the strategic waterway is expected to fully reopen to international shipping and energy transit. (Shady Alassar/Anadolu via Getty Images)

"The regime is relying on tried and true tactics here, which is, you know, a knife in the back and a handshake in the front to many of America's traditional Gulf partners," Taleblu said. "It looks like Iranian escalation, Iranian diplomatic pressure, Iranian diplomatic finesse is trying to back the Trump administration into the MOU again."

"The regime definitely does not want to grant the Trump administration the optics of victory, and to that end, they're quite keen to hold on to the Strait of Hormuz," he added.

Taleblu said Trump has described the sanctions-driven strategy as a "low-key" approach.

"These are high-impact tools," he concluded. "I think part of the escalation that we saw in the summer of 2019 — part of that past could be a prologue."

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

articles.title: Rams star Puka Nacua left bloodied in bizarre accident at Michael Rubin's star-studded White Party
articles.excerpt: OutKick host Dan Dakich joins Stuart Varney to break down the potential $12.5 billion sale of the Los Angeles Lakers to Kushner and Iger, the WNBA's statement on transgender eligibility, and Donald Tr...
articles.body_text:
OutKick host Dan Dakich joins Stuart Varney to break down the potential $12.5 billion sale of the Los Angeles Lakers to Kushner and Iger, the WNBA's statement on transgender eligibility, and Donald Trump's Super Bowl predictions.

Puka Nacua’s turbulent offseason keeps finding new ways to hit him — this time, literally.

The latest bizarre story to emerge from the Los Angeles Rams star’s summer involves a spotless window at Michael Rubin’s "White Party" — and, by Nacua’s own admission, the window won.

Puka Nacua of the Los Angeles Rams reacts during the second quarter against the Indianapolis Colts at SoFi Stadium on Sept. 28, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Ronald Martinez/Getty Images)

During an appearance on Logan Paul’s "Impaulsive" podcast, Nacua revealed that he was left bleeding from the face after walking directly into a glass pane at the Fanatics founder’s annual celebrity bash in the Hamptons.

STEFON DIGGS FOUND NOT GUILTY ON STRANGULATION AND ASSAULT CHARGES, NOW EYES NFL FREE AGENCY

While speaking with Olympic gymnast Suni Lee, Nacua spotted Snoop Dogg and turned to find Rams teammate Davante Adams. He never saw the nearly invisible pane standing in his way.

"Uh, the glass window pane won," Nacua said. And Nacua apparently wasn’t the only victim of Rubin’s spotless glass.

"They made me feel better when they said three other people ran into it," Nacua said. "But nobody else ended up bleeding from it. So I don’t know if that made me feel much better or worse."

Head coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams (R) talks with his defensive coordinator, Wade Phillips before the game against the Baltimore Ravens at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on November 25, 2019 in Los Angeles, California. (Kevork Djansezian/Getty Images)

A run-in with Rubin’s glass is hardly the only headache Nacua has dealt with this offseason. The Rams star is facing a civil lawsuit stemming from a New Year’s Eve incident in which a woman alleges he bit her shoulder and made an antisemitic remark. Nacua’s attorney strongly denies the antisemitic allegation and characterized the biting as "horseplay." The lawsuit followed another controversy involving Nacua, who apologized in December after performing a gesture tied to antisemitic stereotypes during a livestream. He later spent time at a holistic care facility focused on personal growth.

RAMS' SEAN MCVAY AND HIS MODEL WIFE PUT THE REST OF THE NFL ON NOTICE WITH NOTHING BUT SWIMSUITS ON

Nacua’s brother, Samson, was arrested after mistakenly taking an SUV he believed belonged to Puka. Investigators determined it was a mix-up, and Samson was not charged.

Nacua’s offseason could still follow him onto the field, with the NFL reportedly reviewing his conduct and a suspension considered possible. Meanwhile, Nacua gave the Rams a more conventional scare this week when he left Tuesday’s joint practice with the Dallas Cowboys early with groin soreness. He sat out Thursday as Los Angeles took a cautious approach with its All-Pro receiver.

Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua, left, runs against Seattle Seahawks safety Julian Love (20) during the first half of an NFL football game in Seattle, Sunday, Nov. 3, 2024. (AP Photo/Lindsey Wasson)

"We’re just being smart with him," Rams coach Sean McVay said. "Expecting to be back next week, ready to go."

The Rams have every reason to be cautious. Nacua is entering the final season of his rookie contract after leading the NFL with 129 receptions and finishing second with 1,715 receiving yards last season.

McVay and the Rams can manage his practice workload and game-plan for double teams. Billionaire-grade window cleaning is apparently another problem entirely.

Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

Alejandro Avila is a longtime writer at OutKick, living in Southern California.

articles.title: Hasan Piker is becoming the 'face of the progressive movement,' former Democratic operative warns
articles.excerpt:
Evan Barker says campaigning with the controversial Twitch streamer may mobilize progressive voters but risks hurting candidates in competitive states.

Controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker has f...
articles.body_text:
Evan Barker says campaigning with the controversial Twitch streamer may mobilize progressive voters but risks hurting candidates in competitive states.

Controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker has found himself at the center of a debate about the direction of the Democratic Party and generations of voters to come. However, recently on his stream, which he does for hours every day, the far-left commentator has claimed the media is making him out to have more influence than he actually does.

Evan Barker, author of "Nothing Left: Confessions Of A Democratic Operative," disagrees with Piker's analysis of his own popularity — he has more than 3 million followers on Twitch and millions more across other social media accounts — pointing to the increasing number of candidates who have invited him to campaign with them.

"Why would these candidates have this desire to bring him into their state, to campaign alongside him if he wasn't influential, to hold press junkets with him, to invite him to barbecues? Like, why would they be doing that if he didn't have influence? Like, clearly, he does," Barker told Fox News Digital.

Barker is no stranger to Democratic politics. She raised tens of millions of dollars for Democratic candidates, campaigned for Hillary Clinton and worked for candidates backed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y.

EX-DEM OPERATIVE DETAILS 'NEW DONOR ESTABLISHMENT' BEHIND MAMDANI-ERA PROGRESSIVES: 'NOT FROM THE GRASSROOTS'

Former Democrat operative Evan Barker says the party needs to realize that controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker is quickly becoming the face of their movement. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

Barker eventually broke with the party in 2024, a journey she details in her new book. She told Fox News Digital that Democrats are "testing their limits with the popularity" in areas of the country that aren't deep blue, especially when campaigning with Piker.

"It's one thing to appear on somebody's podcast, it's another to have them come campaign for you," she said.

Piker's hours-long stream primarily focuses on politics. He has backed several candidates in the 2026 cycle, including Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed and Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong.

While El-Sayed won his primary race, Hong lost to Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, who has since said he was not planning on campaigning with Piker.

Piker's long history of incendiary and far-left rhetoric has made him an easy target for Republicans. From his retracted comments about saying the U.S. "deserved" 9/11, to his praise of Chinese dictator Mao Zedong, and the hours of talking he does every day, there's no shortage of comments for which Piker and his allies could be held to account.

When asked what she would tell candidates who are thinking about campaigning with the Twitch streamer, Barker told Fox News Digital that she would advise against it.

"I would say that the juice isn't worth the squeeze," she said. "Yeah, you're trying to appeal to younger voters, you're trying to drive out your base, but how do you win a general election aligning with him?"

Former Democrat operative Evan Barker says she would advise candidates to not campaign with Hasan Piker. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

DEMOCRAT ESTABLISHMENT STRIKES BACK AS SOCIALIST CANDIDATE DOWNED IN BATTLEGROUND PRIMARY

While Barker has expressed skepticism about Piker, she said she often hears those on the left defend their relationship with the streamer by comparing him to another media personality: Joe Rogan.

During the 2024 campaign cycle, then-Vice President Kamala Harris was criticized for not appearing on Rogan's show while running for president, particularly after both now-Vice President JD Vance and now-President Donald Trump sat for interviews with him. Some have made the case that Piker could serve as an alternative to Rogan, but Barker disagrees.

"Hasan Piker is not at all like Joe Rogan, actually. So, the charm of Joe Rogan, what makes his show so powerful is that he talks about politics sometimes. Politics is sometimes peppered into his conversations, but by and large, the majority of the time, he's not talking about politics," she said. "Whereas Hasan Piker, that's pretty much all he talks about."

She also noted that some of Piker's rhetoric that appeals to younger voters might not resonate with larger populations in parts of the country that are not deep blue.

"At the end of the day, I would remind these progressive candidates, it's not just about pleasing your staff, it's not just about pleasing, you know, the young people that are in this movement. If you want to win places like Wisconsin, if you want to win places like Michigan, you have to be patriotic," she said. "The Rust Belt is filled with hardworking patriotic Americans who don't feel the way that Hasan Piker does."

Hasan Piker has backed several candidates, including Francesca Hong, who lost Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial primary in August 2026. (Joshua Lott/Getty Images)

WISCONSIN DEMOCRATIC VOTERS CHALK SOCIALIST FRANCESCA HONG'S STUNNING LOSS UP TO ELECTABILITY CONCERNS

As Democrats weigh the consequences of backlash for campaigning with Piker against the access to younger voters that he brings, Barker says the streamer is quickly becoming well known offline as well. She argued that Piker is "probably the biggest podcaster, live streamer" that the Democrats have at their disposal.

"He's quickly becoming a household name. He's quickly becoming the face of the progressive movement," she said.

Barker acknowledged that some progressives may not be "comfortable" with Piker as a de facto leader, calling his rise a "monster that they've created themselves." She also compared the current moment to previous shifts within the progressive movement, arguing that figures and ideas once embraced by the left are later dismissed as excesses of an earlier era.

Twitch streamer Hasan Piker appeared on the campaign trail with Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Barker pointed specifically to recent discussions of "Woke 1" after Ocasio-Cortez's invocation of the term last week, arguing that Democrats have yet to reckon with the consequences of that period around 2020, which was marked by a surge in racial identity politics and progressive groupthink.

"People's lives were ruined because of 'woke 1.' It wasn't just some mass delusion or mass hysteria that we all went through... It pushed people away from Democratic politics," she said.

Barker argued that Democrats' continued willingness to align with figures like Piker shows the party has yet to move beyond that period.

"I think that there needs to be a true reckoning in the progressive movement and in the Democratic Party for people to really be able to heal and move on from this," she said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Piker for comment.

Rachel Wolf is a media and culture reporter for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Who will be the next White House press secretary?
articles.excerpt:
Karoline Leavitt’s abrupt departure has sparked a tough race inside Trump’s circle for the prominent position

Karoline Leavitt’s surprise resignation as the White House press secretary is set to trig...
articles.body_text:
Karoline Leavitt’s abrupt departure has sparked a tough race inside Trump’s circle for the prominent position

Karoline Leavitt’s surprise resignation as the White House press secretary is set to trigger a sharp-elbowed race inside Donald Trump’s world for one of the most prominent positions in the Trump administration.

Several names have circulated since the US president announced that Leavitt would step down at the end of the month to spend more time with her family.

Here are some of the possible contenders.

Cheung currently serves as the White House communications director, and has worked closely with Leavitt throughout the second Trump administration. When he praised the outgoing press secretary for her tenure on Wednesday, Leavitt joked on social media that the pair had survived “many, many news cycles” together.

Habba is a loyal ally of the president who served as his personal lawyer before becoming a short-lived US attorney for New Jersey. A federal judge ultimately ruled her appointment was unlawful.

But Habba has been one of the president’s most vocal defenders on conservative outlets. According to the New York Post, citing sources within the administration, Habba is an early frontrunner to replace Leavitt.

Kelly already works at the White House as the principal deputy press secretary, working under Leavitt. She was previously a spokesperson for Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign, and before that she served as national press secretary for the Republican National Committee.

As the wife of Stephen Miller, a top White House aide and immigration policy architect, Katie Miller has a front row seat to the administration’s movements. And as an influential conservative podcast host, Katie has spent a lot of time interviewing cabinet officials and rightwing media figures.

Before launching her podcast, Katie was a communications director for the so-called “department of government efficiency” (Doge). She was vice-president Mike Pence’s press secretary from 2019 to 2021.

Budowich is a former White House deputy chief of staff, who worked alongside Miller and Dan Scavino. He left the White House last year to join the private sector.

Alongside Leavitt, Budowich was one of the defendants in the case brought by the Associated Press after the outlet was banned from the press rotation for refusing to refer to the Gulf of Mexico as the “Gulf of America”.

articles.title: Sudan army says RSF advance on key town bordering Ethiopia
articles.excerpt: Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces and allies of the paramilitary group have advanced into a strategically important town on the Sudanese border with Ethiopia, military and government sources told Al Jazeer...
articles.body_text:
Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces and allies of the paramilitary group have advanced into a strategically important town on the Sudanese border with Ethiopia, military and government sources told Al Jazeera.

They said the RSF and the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement – North (SPLM-N) entered Kurmuk in Blue Nile State on Thursday, as the army began to withdraw.

An RSF statement said an RSF-led coalition had inflicted heavy losses on army troops in Kurmuk, forced them to withdraw and seized weapons and ammunition.

Hours later, the local administration in Kurmuk said the town had come under intensive attacks over the last three days, involving drones and artillery shelling, which it said originated from “the regional neighbourhood”.

The local administration said the Sudanese army continued to confront the attacks “with steadfastness and bravery” in defence of the town, its residents and public institutions.

The town is on an important cross-border route linking Ethiopia with Blue Nile and the wider Nile Valley.

“The RSF advanced into the town with the army withdrawing and repositioning outside,” Al Jazeera’s Almigdad Alruhaid reported from the Sudanese capital Khartoum, citing military and government sources.

The RSF seized the town in March, but the Sudanese army recaptured it last month.

Sudan has been engulfed in its latest conflict since April 2023, when fighting started between the Sudanese army and the RSF over plans to integrate the paramilitary force into the regular military.

The war has killed tens of thousands of people and displaced or forced nearly 15 million to flee their homes, according to UN figures, local authorities and academic estimates.

Elsewhere in Sudan, the army says it repelled an RSF attack on a major town in North Kordofan.

According to military sources who spoke to Al Jazeera, the paramilitary group assaulted the town of Jabra al-Sheikh using heavy artillery and drones. RSF fighters were captured and dozens were killed in the fight, the sources added.

An army statement said the RSF attack involved more than 250 combat vehicles.

Jabra al-Sheikh is a key transport hub in the region and control of the town could allow the RSF to put pressure on el-Obeid – the capital of North Kordofan – and Omdurman near Khartoum.

The latest attacks come the day after the RSF launched far-reaching coordinated drone strikes targeting five army-controlled cities hundreds of kilometres apart.

Wednesday’s attacks killed two people in el-Obeid and paralysed the city’s market, said the rights group Emergency Lawyers that documents atrocities by both sides.

Across Sudan, aid workers estimate that more than 200,000 people have been killed in what the UN calls a “war of atrocities”. The conflict has also caused the world’s largest hunger and displacement crises.

A passenger train derailed near Lewes in East Sussex, England,  injuring at least 11 people, and two of them seriously. The wreck overturned at least one carriage, trapping several people, as emergency crews responded. The cause of the derailment is being investigated.

articles.title: Surrogate gives birth in Texas to baby with heart defect after parents requested abortion
articles.excerpt: Fox News correspondent Madeleine Rivera reports on a legal battle involving surrogate mother McKenna West, who traveled to Texas to give birth after refusing the intended parents' request to abort the...
articles.body_text:
Fox News correspondent Madeleine Rivera reports on a legal battle involving surrogate mother McKenna West, who traveled to Texas to give birth after refusing the intended parents' request to abort the baby over a congenital heart condition diagnosis.

A surrogate mother gave birth to a baby against its biological parents' wishes after fleeing to Texas with help from state Attorney General Ken Paxton.

Surrogate mother McKenna West fled to Texas after her baby was diagnosed with hypoplastic left heart syndrome around the time West was 20 weeks pregnant. The diagnosis allegedly prompted the baby's birth parents to ask West to have an abortion, Paxton's office wrote in a Tuesday news release.

After West went on the run to Texas, Paxton intervened, formally notifying UT Southwestern Medical Center and Children’s Medical Center of Dallas of their legal obligations to provide the baby with "medically necessary, life-saving care upon birth," his office wrote.

DEM GOV MAURA HEALEY SIGNS SWEEPING MASSACHUSETTS BILL ALLOWING ABORTIONS UP TO BIRTH

July 29, 2015: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton speaks during a hearing in Austin, Texas. ( )

"The court has made the right decision in immediately acting to protect baby Gabriel’s life and ensure he receives the care he deserves," Paxton said in the statement. "My office utilized every tool at our disposal to protect life, and we will not back down in continuing to support baby Gabriel’s well-being. Every child in our state deserves to be cared for and protected, and that’s exactly what I’ll fight for."

"While the surrogate mother of baby Gabriel has traveled to Texas for protection and care for Gabriel, the intended parents have refused to agree that they will consent to the life-saving surgery for Gabriel after he is born. Attorney General Paxton has now secured a legal victory that will ensure baby Gabriel’s life is protected and that care is provided," his office's statement also read.

West's baby, named Gabriel, was born on Wednesday, according to Fox News' Kerri Urbahn. Gabriel was brought to a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit where doctors could soon perform lifesaving surgery.

SUPREME COURT UNANIMOUSLY SLAPS DOWN BLUE STATE TARGETING PRO-LIFE GROUP

Surrogate mother McKenna West, who fled to Texas after her baby's birth parents allegedly asked her to abort the child (Live Action)

The hospital where the surgery would likely be performed has a 100% success rate on the procedure, Urbahn reported.

"Baby Gabriel deserves a chance at life, and I will not allow anyone to unlawfully deny him medically necessary care," Paxton said. "My office will use every tool available to protect innocent lives and ensure that every child receives the care required under Texas law."

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton arrives for the State of the Union address during a Joint Session of Congress at the U.S. Capitol on February 24, 2026, in Washington, DC. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

Fox News Digital contacted Paxton's office, UT Southwestern Medical Center and Children’s Medical Center of Dallas for additional comment.

articles.excerpt: Florida congressional candidate Oliver Larkin faces intense questioning from Sean Hannity over his radical tax policies. During the fiery exchange, the DSA-backed candidate advocates for a return to m...
articles.body_text:
Florida congressional candidate Oliver Larkin faces intense questioning from Sean Hannity over his radical tax policies. During the fiery exchange, the DSA-backed candidate advocates for a return to mid-20th century marginal tax rates and claims that billionaires should be taxed out of existence. Hannity pushes back, defending American innovators and challenging the socialist platform.

The high-stakes battle for the ideological future of the Democratic Party moves to Florida next week, before heading to New England early next month, as the 2026 primary season wraps up.

After impactful left-wing victories this month by Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed and Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan in crucial Democratic Senate primaries, and a searing setback for the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), with the downing of DSA member Francesca Hong in Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial primary, the next faceoff in the party's civil war comes Tuesday in Florida.

That's where DSA endorsed Oliver Larkin is challenging more moderate Democratic Rep. Jared Moskowitz in a key congressional swing district that's among roughly two dozen House seats that will determine if Republicans hold onto their razor-thin majority in the midterm elections.

DEMOCRATIC GROUP LAUNCHES $15 MILLION WAR ON DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS: 'MORTAL DANGER'

Oliver Larkin, a DSA-backed Democratic candidate for Congress in Florida’s 25th district, speaks during a town hall, on May 4, 2026 in Coral Springs, Florida. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)

Two weeks later, the party's divisions return to a statewide stage, as longtime progressive leader Sen. Ed Markey of Massachusetts is facing a serious primary challenge from more moderate Democratic Rep. Seth Moulton.

A left-versus-center battle is brewing a week later in neighboring New Hampshire, in the party's Senate primary for a crucial battleground seat Democrats must hold in the midterm elections in order to win back the chamber's majority from the GOP.

Progressives scored their biggest victory to date a week ago, when El-Sayed narrowly edged moderate Rep. Haley Stevens to capture the party's Senate nomination in the Great Lakes battleground, in the race to succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters.

DEMOCRATIC GROUP LAUNCHES $15 MILLION WAR ON DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS: 'MORTAL DANGER'

Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed speaks to supporters at an election-night rally at the Majestic Theatre in Detroit, Mich., on Aug. 4, 2026. His race against U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens in the state Democratic primary ended too close to call. (Getty Images)

On Tuesday, Flanagan downed moderate Democratic Rep. Angie Craig by roughly 20 points, to grab the party's nomination in blue-leaning but competitive Minnesota, in the race to succeed another retiring Democrat, Sen. Tina Smith.

Both El-Sayed and Flanagan were backed by top far-left leaders, including progressive champion Sen. Bernie Sanders of Vermont.

But in Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial showdown, Hong was upset by a razor-thin margin by Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, who was backed by retiring Democratic Gov. Tony Evers.

Evers and Crowley, pointing to Hong's past controversial comments on defunding the police and criticizing Thanksgiving, argued that a Hong primary victory would have boosted GOP nominee Rep. Tom Tiffany's chances of flipping the Wisconsin governor's mansion.

With the primary calendar winding down, here's a closer look at the final nomination faceoffs that are dividing Democrats and giving Republicans plenty of ammunition to use in the midterms.

The 33-year-old Larkin, a veteran of Sanders' 2016 Democratic presidential campaign, is also the only DSA-endorsed House candidate running in a crucial congressional swing district.

Larkin says he supports abolishing the U.S. Senate, arguing in a Fox News interview that it's an "undemocratic institution."

He agreed with socialist New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu should have been arrested during his recent trip to the U.S., and refers to Israel's ruling coalition as a "religious supremacist regime."

Moskowitz is a strong and vocal supporter of Israel, who has advocated for robust U.S. military and security assistance.

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

Rep. Jared Moskowitz, a Democrat from Florida, faces a primary challenge from the far-left as he runs for re-election in 2026. (Al Drago/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

The two-term federal lawmaker and former state representative and Florida FEMA director is running for re-election in the state's newly redrawn 25th Congressional District, a Broward County-anchored seat in the southeastern corner of the red-leaning state

Moskowitz, who enjoys establishment backing from the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, is also supported by AIPAC, a major-Israel aligned political group. Larkin enjoys plenty of support from top far-left leaders, including controversial political streamer Hasan Piker. Moskowitz is the polling and fundraising lead over Larkin heading into the primary.

Markey is backed by a slew of progressive politicians and groups, including Sanders and Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, as well as fellow Bay Stater Rep. Ayanna Pressley, a member of the far-left Squad.

Sen. Ed Markey of Massachusetts is backed by progressive champions Sens. Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren as he faces a Democratic primary challenge from Rep. Seth Moulton. (Jemal Countess/Getty Images for MoveOn Civic Action)

Moulton is supported by a smaller group of more moderate Democratic lawmakers and groups.

While the primary is partially viewed as a progressive versus moderate showdown, the Democratic Party's generational showdown is very much at play in this contest.

The 80-year-old Markey has served in Congress for half a century, first in the House and since 2013 in the Senate. The 47-year-old Moulton has repeatedly emphasized it's time for a new generation of leaders.

Democratic Rep. Seth Moulton of Massachusetts is primary challenging Sen. Ed Markey in the 2026 election cycle. (Samuel Corum/Getty Images)

The push by Democrats for generational change was fueled two years ago by then-81-year-old President Joe Biden's exit from the presidential race amid questions over his physical and mental stamina following a disastrous debate performance against President Donald Trump.

A similar generational fight is being waged in the Democratic primary in Massachusetts' 8th Congressional District. That's where 71-year-old Rep. Stephen Lynch, who has served in the House for a quarter-century, is being primary challenged by 39-year-old Patrick Roath.

The action moves north a week later to neighboring New Hampshire, where longtime Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, the first woman in the nation's history elected governor and to the Senate, is retiring.

Four-term Rep. Chris Pappas is the front-runner for the Democratic nomination, and enjoys plenty of establishment backing, including from Shaheen and the Granite State's other Democrat in the chamber, Sen. Maggie Hassan.

Democratic Senate candidate in New Hampshire Rep. Chris Pappas is interviewed by Fox News Digital, on July 4, 2025, in Portsmouth, N.H. (Paul Steinhauser - Fox News)

Pappas is the clear polling and fundraising leader in a race that also includes medical scientist Karishma Manzur, who is backed by a handful of progressive groups.

A backer of Israel, Pappas has been blasted over the support he's receiving from AIPAC by Manzur, who argues Israeli has committed "genocide" against Palestinians in its war with Hamas in Gaza.

Fox News' Matthew Donnell contributed to this report.

Paul Steinhauser covers the national campaign trail from coast to coast for Fox News

articles.title: Luxury $9 million yacht caught on camera sinking off coast, days after delivery to owner
articles.excerpt:
The Angiola II sank off the island of Porto Cervo, Sardinia, after an engine fire. (Credit: Jam Press)

A super-luxury $9.1 million yacht sank into the waters of the Mediterranean Sea on Tuesday, just...
articles.body_text:
The Angiola II sank off the island of Porto Cervo, Sardinia, after an engine fire. (Credit: Jam Press)

A super-luxury $9.1 million yacht sank into the waters of the Mediterranean Sea on Tuesday, just days after it had been delivered to its new owner.

The Angiola II was off the coast of Porto Cervo on the popular Italian island of Sardinia with 14 guests on board, when it experienced engine failure that sparked a fire, the New York Post reported.

DRUNK REPEAT OFFENDER CALLED A 'TICKING TIME-BOMB' BEFORE 80-MPH BOATING COLLISION KILLED WOMAN: PROSECUTORS

The Angiola II, a $9.1 million luxury yacht, sank Tuesday in the Mediterranean Sea just days after it had been delivered to its new owner. (Jam Press)

The blaze damaged seals on the vessel, which began to take on water, causing it to tip onto its side. The guests managed to escape to safety and were rescued by nearby vessels, The Telegraph reported.

Video footage taken at the scene shows the boat on its side.

COAST GUARD OPENS FIRE ON BOAT SMUGGLING 25 CHINESE NATIONALS NEAR FLORIDA AFTER IT REFUSED TO STOP

A $9.1 million superyacht sinks in waters off Porto Cervo, Sardinia, just four days after being delivered to its Italian owner. The Angiola II, a nearly 30-meter vessel, lost buoyancy following an engine failure that caused a fire in the seals, allowing water to enter the hull. (Jam Press)

The unidentified owner — an Italian businessman — was the last one off the ship, the newspaper reported.

The yacht reportedly sank at a depth of around 23 feet between an island called L’Isola dei Cappuccini and Capo Ferro, on Sardinia’s exclusive Costa Smeralda, or Emerald Coast, the news report states.

The boat will be kept under surveillance until a recovery company recovers it from the sea floor.

The superyacht sank in the Mediterranean Sea off Porto Cervo, Sardinia. Fourteen people were on board; 12 were rescued by a nearby vessel, while the owner and a friend remained on the yacht until a patrol boat transported them to Poltu Quatu. No injuries were reported. (Jam Press)

The yacht can reportedly accommodate 10 guests and is fitted with five cabins and five crew members.

It has four engines and can reach speeds of 28 knots.

Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

articles.title: Baseball fans fume at MLB's 'Field of Dreams' game decision, reporter Tricia Whitaker has a boat day & LLWS!
articles.excerpt:
Three fans ran onto the field at Yankee Stadium on Wednesday and were promptly wrestled to the ground in a chaotic scene. (This video contains AI-assisted content)

'Nightcaps' is a daily column that ...
articles.body_text:
Three fans ran onto the field at Yankee Stadium on Wednesday and were promptly wrestled to the ground in a chaotic scene. (This video contains AI-assisted content)

'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com.

Over the hump and safely into a big Thursday filled with actual NFL football (kind of) and an MLB Field of Dreams game only the 1%ers can watch.

What a blessing. What a day! Are things starting to ramp up, or what? And who knows! Maybe by the end of this class, the WNBA will have figured out what a woman is.

HOME RUN DERBY RATINGS CRASH ON NETFLIX, SETS 20-PLUS-YEAR LOW AS QUESTIONS SURFACE ABOUT PROGRAM QUALITY

I wouldn't hold your breath, but there's always a chance.

Welcome to a Thursday Nightcaps — the one where Pat Sajak, of all people, points out the lunacy in tonight's annual Field of Dreams game.

Players from the Chicago White Sox and New York Yankees walk through the corn rows before a game at Field of Dreams in Dyersville, Iowa, on Aug. 12, 2021. (Getty Images)

Pat Sajak! We usually only check in with Maggie Sajak in this class. I believe Pat's a first-timer. Welcome aboard!

What else? I've got a couple wild moments yesterday in the world of little league baseball, Apple TV's Tricia Whitaker enjoyed a Canadian cottage getaway and Lordy, did you guys have some steak takes on the heels of yesterday's class.

Take out a second mortgage, grab you a Netflix subscription and settle in for a Thursday 'Cap!

I think Major League Baseball does a lot of things right. Frankly, they're probably the best sport when it comes to doing things that make sense.

Look at the mess that is the WNBA right now and compare it to MLB. It's laughable.

The pitch clock was brilliant. I've come around on the ghost runner. ABS has very clearly worked. The Home Run Derby and the All-Star game are the two best exhibition events in sports (not a high bar, to be fair).

The Field of Dreams game has been a home run since its debut way back in 2021. It's perfect. Everything about it is perfect.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

This year — tonight — is the first year it won't be on Fox. Instead, it was scooped up by Netflix during last year's TV negotiations.

Yes, that means if you really want to watch some Phillies-Twins action tonight from Iowa, you're gonna have to pay up.

Does it seem a bit ironic that MLB’s Field of Dreams game — which harkens back to a simpler, more bucolic time — is being streamed on Netflix?

You know what, Pat Sajak? You are 1000% right. What a rip-off! More importantly, what a vocabulary on 79-year-old Pat Sajak! Bucolic? I'm not sure I've ever seen that word in my life. Does Pat still have the fastball, or what?

Bucolic, by the way, is an adjective that means relating to the pleasant, peaceful aspects of the countryside, country life, or shepherds, according to the stupid AI bot that runs Google now.

Pat wasn't alone in his bewilderment, by the way:

I could go on and on. Nobody is happy. Is anyone ever happy?

For those still on the fence, a Netflix subscription costs $8.99 a month (with ads). If you really hate ads, you have to pony up a whopping $20 a month. And if you really hate ads AND regular 1080p HD, you have to pay $27 for the 4K version.

Thank God I'm a T-Mobile customer. Free MLB TV and Netflix included! What a deal.

(Not a promotion, but I wouldn't mind if it was.)

Aaron Judge #99 of the New York Yankees hits a three-run home run in the third inning during a game against the Chicago White Sox at the MLB Field at Field of Dreams on Thursday, Aug. 12, 2021, in Dyersville, Iowa. (MLB Photos via Getty Images)

OK, let's keep this class moving ... from the big diamond to the little diamond! What a night we had in the Little League World Series regionals last night.

The coach who gave a sermon on the mound (come on, that's a good one!) is taking a little heat today because folks say he should've been out there giving a scouting report instead. Boots on the ground say the next three batters reached safely, and Arizona went on to lose.

Not great! For what it's worth, my little league coach used to tell me, "Zach, if you strike out, there are a billion people in China who will wake up tomorrow and won't care."

Decent advise for a 12-year-old, I reckon. But we also never got anywhere close to Williamsport, so perhaps we could've used some more motivation.

Garrett Gallegos #19 of the Mountain Region from Las Vegas, Nevada reacts before the sixth inning against the Asia-Pacific Region team from Taoyuan City, Chinese Taipei during the 2025 Little League World Series Championship at Howard J. Lamade Stadium on Aug. 24, 2025, in South Williamsport, Pa. (Getty Images)

As for the coach who got tossed ... that's nothing. I grew up with a coach who used to get thrown out every week for arguing anything and everything under the sun. During one All-Star game in particular, he snuck back into the complex Bobby Valentine style and hung out behind the outfield fence.

That's called commitment. Loved Coach Tony.

OK, let's rapid-fire this Thursday class into a big Thursday night of preseason football. First up? Yesterday, I gave you my Mount Rushmore of Steaks to celebrate National Filet Mignon Day.

Anything that moos is my favorite meat. I grew up a meat and potatoes kid. Still am 7 decades later. Ribeyes and Kansas City strips are my favorites. My smoker will be fired up this weekend.

Thanks, Larry! Bring a couple over to the Field of Dreams game!

Ribeye on the bone — the bone must be there with no questions asked – it’s not the same eating a boneless ribeye.

Porterhouse — which you cannot go wrong, and it is of course two steaks in one on a big bone — so technically, number 2 and 3 would equal a porterhouse.

Thanks, Tom! Agree wholeheartedly on the bone-in Ribeye. Huge difference.

Agree with your steak rankings. Up until end of last year I never even considered ordering anything but a ribeye, but I’ve been on a filet tear so far this year. For me it’s more about portion control than anything else. I can’t be knocking down 14+ oz ribeyes all the time anymore.

It's football season, Ryan. Portion control, shmortion control! Let's get the ribeyes back in the rotation and worry about the waistline in January.

OK, that's it for today. Good work, everyone. Six NFL preseason games tonight and the Field of Dreams game for those who have a rich uncle who recently kicked the bucket.

Here's Apple TV's MLB girl, Tricia Whitaker, to get everyone ready.

Best little league memories? Email me at Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.
